bottleneck_breakdown.python_loop_overhead: ~140ms per observation iteration (3 SourceCursor file reads + 4 process polls)

conclusion: External Driver file-based orchestration CANNOT achieve the timely case within 150ms. This is an architectural constraint (Python loop + fsync I/O), not a single bug.
fix_options: A: Pre-position action on job_received trigger (~1ms before boundary, path committed by entry)
B: In-process trigger (Worker executes path action itself via DDS)
C: Real-time signal file (not JSONL, minimal I/O)
D: Relax to accept expired case as valid T2-B evidence (controversial)
recommendation: Option A: job_received trigger with boundary_entered as the in-flight PROOF (not trigger). The path change is pre-positioned; boundary_entered proves the Job was held; release proves the C call happened after the path change; the Regulator rejection proves version mismatch. This preserves all semantic requirements while eliminating the timing constraint.
